mission.title: clickhouse: SQL with pipes
mission.description: SQL with pipes. Requested by 23+ users.

steps.title: Check current clickhouse setup
steps.description:
Verify your clickhouse version and configuration:
```bash
clickhouse-client --version
```
This feature requires a working clickhouse installation.

steps.title: Review clickhouse configuration
steps.description:
Review the relevant clickhouse configuration:
Recent work by Google [1] argues that SQL is not user-friendly because you can't read it top-down. E.g. processing starts at the "bottom" in the FROM clause or in subqueries (but there are more problems).

steps.title: Apply the fix for SQL with pipes
steps.description:
It can be implemented in a much simpler way:

Do not use ZetaSQL, and do not introduce a new dialect - reuse the ClickHouse parser instead.

Add `|>` operator to the Lexer.

Add `ParserPipelinedQuery` to the parser, which parses both sides of the operator in a way similar to SELECT queries, in a left-associative fashion, where each step generates an AST as a chain of subqueries with corresponding transformations.

`ParserPipelinedQuery` will be accepted as an alternative to `ParserSelectQuery`

See the source issue for community-verified solutions.

steps.description:
